sentences.text: Archaeoceratops was a small, bipedal dinosaur with a light body adapted for fast walking. It could switch between standing on two legs and walking on four.
This primitive ceratopsian featured a large head with a small bony frill at the back of its skull, but it lacked horns.
Although exact measurements vary, scientists estimate the animal was about one meter in length.
This species holds the record for being one of the smallest known ceratopsians, weighing only ten kilograms.
Its unique ability to adopt both bipedal and quadrupedal stances set it apart from many other dinosaurs of its time.
Fossils were uncovered in the Gongpoquan Basin of Gansu Province, north central China, within the Xinminbao Group.
Dong Zhiming and Azuma first named the type species Archaeoceratops oshimai in 1996, formally describing it in 1997.
A second species, A. yujingziensis, was later identified based on distinct details in the jaw and teeth.
As a herbivore, Archaeoceratops likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers, since flowering plants were geographically limited during the Cretaceous.
In 1997, the researchers placed Archaeoceratops in the new family Archaeoceratopsidae.
This dinosaur lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 140 to 130 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
